name: Amr ibn Kulthum
bio: Amr ibn Kulthum ibn Malik ibn Attab, of the tribe of Taghlib, was a pre-Islamic poet of the first rank, in al-Zirikli's words, born in the north of the Arabian peninsula among the tribes of Rabi'a and a traveller through Syria, Iraq and Najd. His mother was Layla, daughter of Muhalhil and niece of Kulayb, and al-Aghani reports from the genealogist al-Akhdhar that he became chief of his people at fifteen. He is the man who killed Amr ibn Hind, king of al-Hira: the king had his mother Hind try to make Layla wait on her, Layla cried out to Taghlib for help, and Amr seized the king's sword from where it hung in the tent and struck him on the head, after which Taghlib plundered the royal tent and rode off to al-Jazira, as al-Aghani tells it. His best-known poem is his Mu'allaqa, and the poet al-Attabi was one of his descendants. Al-Akhdhar says he died at a hundred and fifty, and al-Zirikli that he died in the Euphrates region of al-Jazira about 40 years before the Hijra (around 584 CE).
